standard_prerequisites.name: Amalgamation in a bound
standard_prerequisites.statement: A$\leq$n B means that the extension absorbs any set of at most n new elements.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the bound that the proposition makes explicit.

standard_prerequisites.name: Two HF-orderings combined
standard_prerequisites.statement: An HF-ordering of C can be concatenated with the restriction of an HF-ordering of B* to the complement of C to give an HF-ordering of the union.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the construction that produces the amalgam.

standard_prerequisites.name: Isomorphic copy over A
standard_prerequisites.statement: B* is a copy of B fixing A, arranged so that the union with C is unconfined.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the choice made at the start of the proof.

core_obligations: Assume A elementary in B and A n plus the size of B minus A elementary in C, choose a copy B* of B over A such that the union with C is disjoint enough, and let D be that union (source line 742).

Show that D carries an HF-ordering with C as an initial segment, by concatenating an HF-ordering of C with the restriction of an HF-ordering of B*, and check the failure case produces two blocks with smaller elements already in the union (source lines 744-746).
Finally check the bounded condition for B* in D: take a subset of D outside B* of size at most n and use the two hypotheses together with the previous item to conclude (source line 748).

proof_roadmap.step: Build the amalgam and put an HF-ordering on it with C initial.
Verify the HF condition by analysing the failure case.
Check the bounded condition for the amalgam.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 740-741: the class of unconfined Steiner triple systems has the bounded amalgamation property for every bound, and in fact the bound can be taken to be the prescribed one plus the number of elements of B outside A. The proof (source lines 742-749) constructs the amalgam rather than citing one: it picks a copy of B over A arranged so that the union with C is unconfined, shows that the union carries an HF-ordering with C as initial segment by concatenating two orderings and analysing the failure case, and only then verifies the bounded condition for the copy inside the amalgam using the two hypotheses. The statement records the property and the explicit bound, and none of the construction.
